column2:
hablé
Yesterday I spoke with María · -ar yo: -é, and the stress lands on it

trabajamos
Last week we worked a lot · -ar nosotros is identical to the present: only the time word tells you which

empezó
What time did the class start yesterday? · él: -ó, with the accent

jugué
Last night I played football · g → gu before é, to keep the hard sound

column1: Ayer ___ las llaves media hora. (buscar — yo)
column2:
busqué
Yesterday I looked for the keys for half an hour · c → qu before é

toqué
On Monday I played the piano · c → qu before é, same as busqué

encontraste
Did you find the book? · no stem change in the past: encontraste, never encuentraste

necesitaron
They needed more time · -ar ellos: -aron

llevé
I wore a black T-shirt · regular -ar

pensaste
What were you thinking about? · pensar loses its ie in the past: pensaste

comí
Yesterday I ate paella · -er/-ir yo: -í

bebiste
What did you drink last night? · -iste for tú, with no accent

vivió
She lived in Seville for two years · él: -ió

volvimos
We came home late · volver drops its ue here: volvimos

column1: Ellos ___ de casa a las ocho. (salir)
column2:
salieron
They left home at eight · -ieron for ellos

perdí
I missed the train · perder is regular in the past: perdí

durmió
He slept for eight hours · o → u in él and ellos only: durmió, durmieron

pidieron
They asked for the bill · e → i in él and ellos only: pidió, pidieron

visteis
Did you all see the match? · ver takes the plain endings with no accents

conocí
I met Ana in 2020 · conocer in the past means met for the first time

tuve
Yesterday I had an exam · tuv- + e · no accent: tuve, never tuvé

tuvo
She had to work on Sunday · tuvo que + infinitive

estuviste
Where were you last night? · estuv- + iste

estuvimos
We were in Madrid for three days · a finished stretch of time → estar in the preterite

pudimos
We couldn't go · pud- + imos

dijeron
They told the truth · a j stem takes -eron, not -ieron: dijeron

hiciste
What did you do on Saturday? · hic- + iste

hizo
He made dinner last night · c → z in él only: hizo

puso
She set the table · pus- + o, with no accent

vinieron
My friends came to the party · vin- + ieron

supe
I didn't know any of that · sup- + e · in the past supe often means I found out

trajo
He brought the dessert · traj- + o · ellos: trajeron, not trajieron

quise
I wanted to go, but I couldn't · quis- + e

Hubo
There were a lot of people at the party · hubo is the past of hay, and never goes plural

fue
Yesterday was a perfect day · ser: fui, fuiste, fue

column1: El año pasado ___ a México. (ir — nosotros)
column2:
fuimos
Last year we went to Mexico · ser and ir share this form; only the sentence tells you which

fuiste
When did you go to Spain? · fuiste is both you went and you were

vi
I watched TV last night · vi, with no accent - one syllable needs none

dio
My father gave me a book · dar borrows the -er endings: di, diste, dio

gustó
I really liked the film · me gustó + one thing

gustaron
We really liked the tapas · a plural thing → gustaron

Ayer trabajé desde casa.
ayer marks a finished moment → preterite

column1: Last night we ate at a restaurant.
column2:
Anoche comimos en un restaurante.
anoche = last night

column1: Last week I saw my friends.
column2:
La semana pasada vi a mis amigos.
la semana pasada · the personal a before people

column1: Last year they went to Spain.
column2:
El año pasado fueron a España.
fueron = they went, and also they were

¿Qué hiciste ayer?
no helper verb: the past is in hiciste alone

No pude venir.
pude + infinitive · no goes before the verb

Me dijo la verdad.
me dijo = she told me · the pronoun still comes first

Tuvieron un problema.
tuv- + ieron · problema is masculine

column1: It was a very good day.
column2:
Fue un día muy bueno.
fue for a finished whole: the day is over

Conocí a mi mujer en 2015.
conocí = I met (for the first time)

Nos levantamos temprano.
the reflexive pronoun stays in front: nos levantamos

¿Te gustó la comida?
te gustó + one thing

Le di las llaves.
le = to him · di, with no accent

column1: Two years ago I lived in Barcelona.
column2:
Hace dos años viví en Barcelona.
hace + time = ago

Volvió a casa tarde.
volvió, not vuelvió

Empecé a trabajar a las ocho.
z → c before é: empecé

Pidieron la cuenta.
pedir: pidió, pidieron in the third person

Jugué al tenis el sábado.
jugué · jugar a + sport

Dormimos muy bien.
dormimos is both we sleep and we slept

column1: I was at home all day.
column2:
Estuve en casa todo el día.
a finished stretch → estuve · todo el día = all day

corrí
Yesterday I ran ten kilometres · regular -er: corrí

nadé
Last summer I swam a lot · regular -ar: nadé

llamé
I called you three times yesterday · tres veces = three times

llegué
I arrived late to the meeting · g → gu before é: llegué

llegasteis
What time did you all arrive? · only the yo form changes its spelling

column1: Ellos ___ las fotos toda la tarde. (mirar)
column2:
miraron
They looked at the photos all afternoon · regular -ar: miraron

creyó
Nobody believed my story · i → y between vowels: creyó, creyeron

creímos
We didn't believe any of it · the í keeps its accent: creí, creímos

aprendí
I learnt a lot in Spain · regular -er

Oíste
Did you hear the noise last night? · oíste, with the accent

oyeron
They didn't hear anything · i → y: oyó, oyeron

siguió
He kept studying in Madrid · e → i in él and ellos: siguió, siguieron

column1: Yo ___ dos libros el mes pasado. (leer)
column2:
leí
I read two books last month · leí, with the accent

leyó
She read the letter twice · leyó, leyeron with a y

Ayer corrí cinco kilómetros.
ayer + preterite

Anoche me llamó.
me llamó · the pronoun stays before the verb

Llegaron tarde.
llegaron · only llegué changes its spelling

column1: I read that book last year.
column2:
Leí ese libro el año pasado.
leí = I read (past) · leo = I read (present)
